key_insight: The paper argues that verifiable environments can be built like LEGO bricks: smaller, trustworthy tasks can be recursively composed into much larger environments for RL training. This enables reasoning generalization without relying on slow, hand-crafted environment creation.
problem_solved: Existing verifiable-environment construction is mostly manual or one-off, so scaling it increases linearly and becomes a bottleneck for training LLMs at breadth and complexity.
method: Introduces RACES (Recursive Automated Composition for Environment Scaling), a framework for building new environments by composing existing verifiable components.
Uses recursive composition to generate larger, more complex training environments while preserving verifiability.
Aims to scale environment diversity efficiently so RL can improve reasoning generalization beyond a small set of handcrafted tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path to scale RL training data for reasoning without proportional increases in human design effort. It could make environment generation more efficient, reusable, and extensible for building stronger LLM reasoning systems.
visual_elements: A LEGO-brick style diagram showing small verified tasks combining into larger environments
A pipeline graphic for RACES: seed environments -> recursive composition -> scaled training set

paper_title: Verifiable Environments Are LEGO Bricks: Recursive Composition for Reasoning Generalization
paper_authors: Hao Xiang, Qiaoyu Tang, Le Yu, Yaojie Lu, Xianpei Han
